summary: Count aloud to 100 by ones and tens, and count back from 10 to 0.
Count up to 100 by ones starting from any number below 100.
Write numerals 0 to 20 and show each amount with objects (0 means none).
Link counting to how many: one number per object, last number is the total.
Count up to 20 arranged objects (10 scattered) and draw a set to match a numeral.
Tell whether one group of up to 10 objects has more, fewer or the same.
Compare two written numbers from 0 to 10 without using inequality symbols.
Show adding and taking away within 10 with objects, fingers, pennies, drawings, sounds or equations.
Solve addition and subtraction story problems within 10 using objects or drawings.
Split numbers up to 10 into two parts in different ways and record each split.
Find the partner that makes 10 for any number 0 to 10 and record it.
Add and subtract within 5 fluently.
Copy and continue simple patterns made with real objects.
Build and break apart 11 to 19 as ten ones plus some more ones.
Sort up to 10 objects into categories, count and order them; use Venn diagrams, pictographs, yes-no charts.
Name and describe measurable features of one object, such as length, weight or height.
Compare two objects side by side to see which has more or less of an attribute.
Name shapes of everyday objects and describe where they are using position words.
Name shapes correctly no matter their size or which way they face.
Tell whether a shape is flat (two-dimensional) or solid (three-dimensional).
Compare flat and solid shapes informally by sides, corners and other features.
Build shapes from sticks, clay or other materials and draw them.
Put simple shapes together to make bigger shapes.
Solve addition and subtraction story problems within 20 of each type, using an unknown symbol.
Solve story problems adding three whole numbers with a total of 20 or less.
Use properties such as order and grouping as strategies to add and subtract.
Treat subtraction as finding a missing addend.
Connect counting on and back to adding and subtracting.
Add and subtract within 20, fluent within 10 using counting on, making ten and related facts.
Know the equal sign means the same as and judge addition or subtraction equations true or false.
Find the missing whole number anywhere in an addition or subtraction equation.
Copy, extend and make up patterns and number sequences with various materials.
Count forward and backward to 120 from any number; read, write and represent numbers to 120.
Explain that a two-digit number is made of tens and ones, including teen numbers and decades.
Compare two-digit numbers by tens and ones using >, = and <.
Add within 100 with models and place-value strategies, sometimes making a ten, and explain.
Find 10 more or 10 less than a two-digit number mentally and explain why.
Subtract multiples of 10 from multiples of 10 (10 to 90) with models and explain.
Organize and read data in up to three categories, including Venn diagrams, pictographs and yes-no charts.
Order three objects by length and compare two lengths using a third object.
Measure length in whole non-standard units laid end to end without gaps or overlaps.
Tell and write time to the hour and half hour on analog and digital clocks.
Name pennies and dimes and know what each is worth.
Separate defining from non-defining features of shapes and build or draw shapes with given features.
Combine flat or solid shapes into a composite shape, then make new shapes from it.
Split circles and rectangles into halves and fourths; more shares means smaller shares.
Solve one- and two-step addition and subtraction story problems within 100 with drawings and equations.
Add and subtract within 20 fluently with mental strategies; know all one-digit sums automatically.
Decide with objects whether up to 20 items is even or odd; write doubles equations.
Find totals in arrays up to 5 by 5 by repeated addition and write the equation.
Copy, extend, make up and describe patterns and sequences with various materials.
Explain hundreds, tens and ones in three-digit numbers, including 100 as ten tens.
Count within 1,000 by ones, fives, tens and hundreds.
Read and write numbers to 1,000 as numerals, number names and expanded form.
Compare two three-digit numbers by place value using >, = and <.
Add and subtract within 100 fluently using place-value and property-based strategies.
Add up to four two-digit numbers using a variety of strategies.
Add and subtract within 1,000 with models and place value, regrouping when needed; link to written work.
Mentally add or subtract 10 or 100 for numbers from 100 to 900.
Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work using place value and properties.
Measure several objects to the nearest whole unit and show the lengths on a line plot.
Make picture and bar graphs (up to four categories), solve problems, and predict from Venn diagrams or charts.
Measure length with rulers, yardsticks, meter sticks or tape measures.
Measure an object in two units and explain how the results relate to unit size.
Estimate lengths in inches, feet, centimeters and meters.
Measure how much longer one object is than another in standard units.
Solve length story problems within 100 using drawings or equations with an unknown.
Draw whole-number number lines and use them to show sums and differences within 100.
Tell time to the nearest five minutes with a.m. and p.m.; use quarter past, half past, quarter to.
Name nickels and quarters, total coin collections, and solve money problems within one dollar using cent signs.
Identify triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons and cubes; draw shapes with given angles or faces.
Split a rectangle into rows and columns of equal squares and count them.
Split circles and rectangles into halves, thirds or fourths; equal shares can differ in shape.
Show a product of whole numbers as equal groups and write it as an expression.
Interpret a quotient as the size of each share or the number of shares.
Solve multiplication and division story problems within 100 with models and equations.
Find the missing number in a multiplication or division equation.
Use properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide.
Think of division as a multiplication problem with a missing factor.
Multiply and divide within 100 fluently; know all one-digit products automatically by year end.
Solve two-step story problems with all four operations and check answers by estimating.
Spot arithmetic patterns and explain them using properties of operations.
Round whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100 using place value.
Add and subtract within 1,000 fluently using various strategies.
Multiply a one-digit number by a multiple of ten from 10 to 90 with models.
Explain a unit fraction as one equal part of a whole and other fractions as counts of them.
Place unit and other fractions on a number line from 0 to 1 and beyond.
Explain equivalent fractions, write whole numbers as fractions, and compare fractions with same numerator or denominator.
Make scaled picture and bar graphs, solve how-many-more problems, and find a simple probability from a picture.
Measure to the half and quarter inch and show the data on a line plot.
Tell time to the minute and solve elapsed-time problems in minutes on a number line.
Estimate and measure liquid volume and mass in liters, grams and kilograms; solve one-step problems.
Find the area of a rectangle with whole-number sides by tiling and counting unit squares.
Measure area by counting unit squares in metric, customary or made-up units.
Connect area to multiplication and the distributive property through real problems and models.
Find areas of rectilinear shapes by breaking them into rectangles.
Build rectangles with equal perimeters but different areas, or equal areas but different perimeters.
Solve perimeter problems for polygons, including a missing side of a rectangle.
Describe polygons up to eight sides, triangles and quadrilaterals by sides and square corners; draw examples.
Read and write equations as multiplicative comparisons, such as times as many.
Solve multiplicative comparison story problems with drawings and equations.
Solve multi-step story problems, interpret remainders, write equations and check by estimating.
Find factor pairs for 1 to 100, recognize multiples, and tell prime from composite.
Generate a number or shape pattern from a rule and study its features.
Explain that each place is worth ten times the place to its right.
Read and write multi-digit whole numbers in standard, word and expanded form.
Compare two multi-digit whole numbers with >, = and < using place value.
Round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.
Add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers fluently, linking strategies to the standard algorithm.
Multiply up to four digits by one digit and two-digit by two-digit numbers with models.
Divide up to four-digit numbers by one digit with remainders, using arrays, area models or equations.
Use models to explain and generate equivalent fractions.
Compare fractions with unlike parts using benchmarks or common denominators; record with symbols.
Split fractions into unit fractions; add and subtract like-denominator fractions and mixed numbers, including stories.
Multiply a whole number by a fraction with models and solve related story problems.
Show tenths and hundredths are equivalent and add fractions with denominators 10 and 100.
Write tenths and hundredths fractions as decimals using models.
Compare decimals to hundredths with models and symbols, justifying the result.
Solve problems from picture graphs, bar graphs and line plots, including fraction line plots.
Pick suitable units and convert larger units to smaller ones in one system using a table.
Solve measurement story problems on distance, time, volume, mass and money with all four operations.
Use area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real and math problems.
Recognize an angle as two rays sharing an endpoint.
Measure angles in whole degrees with a protractor and sketch angles of a given size.
Show angle measures add when an angle is split, and find unknown angles.
Draw and find points, lines, segments, rays, angle types, and parallel or perpendicular lines.
Classify flat shapes by parallel or perpendicular sides or angle types; identify right triangles.
Recognize line symmetry and draw lines of symmetry.
Write, explain and evaluate expressions with grouping symbols for up to two-step problems.
Make two rule-based patterns in an input/output table, relate terms, and graph the ordered pairs.
Explain place values as ten times or one tenth of neighbors; use powers of ten patterns.
Read, write and compare decimals to thousandths, including expanded form.
Round decimals to any place through thousandths.
Multiply multi-digit whole numbers fluently with the standard algorithm.
Divide up to four-digit numbers by two-digit numbers using place-value strategies and models.
Add, subtract, multiply and divide decimals to hundredths with models and explain the method.
Solve fraction addition and subtraction story problems, using benchmarks to check reasonableness.
Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with unlike denominators using equivalent fractions.
See fractions as division and solve division stories with fraction or mixed-number answers.
Multiply fractions by whole numbers or fractions, including areas of rectangles with fraction sides.
Treat multiplication as scaling and predict product size from the other factor.
Solve real problems multiplying fractions and mixed numbers with models or equations.
Divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions, with stories and models.
Make line plots of fraction measurements and solve problems using the data.
Convert units within one measurement system and use them in multi-step problems.
Understand volume and measure it by counting unit cubes in standard or made-up units.
Find rectangular prism volumes with l x w x h or B x h, including two-prism solids.
Plot points in the first quadrant and interpret coordinates in real and math problems.
Classify triangles by side lengths and by angle types.
Sort quadrilaterals into a hierarchy by their properties.
Explain that subcategories share all attributes of their larger category of shapes.

state_code: # - 2019 Alabama Course of Study: Mathematics (ALSDE), K-5 content standards pp. 18-56:
# - Current for 2026-27: ALSDE Mathematics page (https://www.alabamaachieves.org/content-areas-specialty/mathematics/, checked 2026-10-01)
#   still links only the "2019 Alabama Course of Study" above. Searches found no draft, public-comment call or adoption of a newer
#   math COS (2025-26 ALSDE revisions/public comment were for CTE, digital literacy/CS, world languages, health). Not definitive: ALSDE
#   has no single dated "in effect" list for math; if a new math COS was adopted after Sept 2026 it would not take effect before 2027-28.
# - Official crosswalks: none found. The 2019 COS has no CCSS identifiers and its appendices (A-G) are teaching practices,
#   pathways, resources, HS requirements, homework - no K-5 alignment table. The Feb 2019 SBOE presentation
#   shows a draft layout with bracketed CCSS ids (e.g. grade 1 std 22 [1.G.3], grade 3 std 13 [3.NF.1]) but those were dropped
#   from the adopted text. No ALSDE 2016-to-2019 K-5 crosswalk was found. All mappings here are my own reading against CCSS text.
# - The COS numbers content standards 1..N within each grade under a grade heading ("Kindergarten Content Standards",
#   "Grade 1 Content Standards"...), e.g. grade 1 standard "20." ; sub-standards are a, b, c, d (required). No prefix in the document.
# - Here: AL.<grade>.<n> (AL.K.3, AL.1.20). Sub-parts are folded into their standard. Counts: K 23, 1 23, 2 27, 3 26, 4 29, 5 23.
# - Student Mathematical Practices (8, same as CCSS SMPs) skipped.
# CONTENT AREAS AND CLUSTERS (official names; note AL uses "Operations with Numbers: Base Ten/Fractions", not "Number and Operations...")
# - K: Foundations of Counting (Know number names and the count sequence; Count to tell the number of objects; Compare numbers);
#   Operations and Algebraic Thinking (Understand addition as putting together and adding to, and subtraction as taking apart and
#   taking from; Understand simple patterns); Operations with Numbers: Base Ten (Work with numbers 11-19 to gain foundations for place
#   value); Data Analysis (Collect and analyze data and interpret results); Measurement (Describe and compare measurable attributes);
#   Geometry (Identify and describe shapes; Analyze, compare, create, and compose shapes).
# - Grade 1: OA (Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction; Understand and apply properties of operations and
#   the relationship between addition and subtraction; Add and subtract within 20; Work with addition and subtraction equations;
#   Understand simple patterns); Base Ten (Extend the counting sequence; Understand place value; Use place value understanding and
#   properties of operations to add and subtract); Data Analysis (Collect and analyze data and interpret results); Measurement
#   (Describe and compare measurable attributes; Work with time and money); Geometry (Reason with shapes and their attributes).
# - Grade 2: OA (Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction; Add and subtract within 20; Work with equal groups
#   of objects to gain foundations for multiplication; Understand simple patterns); Base Ten (Understand place value; Use place value
#   understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract); Data Analysis (Collect and analyze data and interpret results);
#   Measurement (Measure and estimate lengths in standard units; Relate addition and subtraction to length; Work with time and money);
#   Geometry (Reason with shapes and their attributes).
# - Grade 3: OA (Represent and solve problems involving multiplication and division; Understand properties of multiplication and the
#   relationship between multiplication and division; Multiply and divide within 100; Solve problems involving the four operations,
#   and identify and explain patterns in arithmetic); Base Ten (Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform
#   multi-digit arithmetic); Fractions (Develop understanding of fractions as numbers); Data Analysis (Represent and interpret data);
#   Measurement (Solve problems involving measurement and estimation of intervals of time, liquid volumes, and masses of objects;
#   Geometric measurement: area; Geometric measurement: perimeter); Geometry (Reason with shapes and their attributes).
# - Grade 4: OA (Solve problems with whole numbers using the four operations; Gain familiarity with factors and multiples; Generate
#   and analyze patterns); Base Ten (Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit whole numbers; Use place value understanding
#   and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic with whole numbers); Fractions (Extend understanding of fraction
#   equivalence and ordering; Build fractions from unit fractions...; Understand decimal notation for fractions, and compare decimal
#   fractions); Data Analysis (Represent and interpret data); Measurement (Solve problems involving measurement and conversion of
#   measurements from a larger unit to a smaller unit; Geometric measurement: understand concepts of angle and measure angles);
#   Geometry (Draw and identify lines and angles, and identify shapes by properties of their lines and angles).
# - Grade 5: OA (Write and interpret numerical expressions; Analyze patterns and relationships); Base Ten (Understand the place value
#   system; Perform operations with multi-digit whole numbers and decimals to hundredths); Fractions (Use equivalent fractions as a
#   strategy to add and subtract fractions; Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to multiply and
#   divide fractions); Data Analysis (Represent and interpret data); Measurement (Convert like measurement units within a given
#   measurement system; Geometric measurement: volume); Geometry (Graph points on the coordinate plane...; Classify two-dimensional
#   figures into categories based on their properties).
# - None outright. 3.G.A.2 (partition shapes into equal areas, each a unit fraction) has no geometry standard (grade 3 geometry is only AL.3.26);
#   it is mapped to AL.3.13, whose unit fraction is one part of an equally partitioned area model. Every CCSS K-5 standard maps to some AL standard.
# - Patterns strand in K-2 ("Understand simple patterns"): AL.K.13, AL.1.9, AL.2.5 (new).
# - Counting backward: from 10 in K (AL.K.1), within 120 in grade 1 (AL.1.10).
# - Data displays: Venn diagrams, pictographs and yes-no charts in K-2 (AL.K.15a, AL.1.16b, AL.2.16b with predicting an outcome);
#   simple probability from a picture in grade 3 (AL.3.16a); picture/bar graph interpretation kept in grade 4 (AL.4.20).
# - Money: pennies and dimes in grade 1 (AL.1.20, moved from 2.MD.C.8); pennies used for representing addition in K (AL.K.8);
#   grade 2 money limited to coins within one dollar, no decimal notation (AL.2.24).
# - Triangle classification by sides and angles (isosceles/equilateral/scalene; acute/obtuse/right/equiangular) in grade 5 (AL.5.21).
# - Fluency/automaticity statements: state all one-digit sums automatically by end of grade 2 (AL.2.2a), products by end of grade 3 (AL.3.7b).
# - kind judged on content: same = CCSS content reworded, split or with small added examples; edited = notable addition or limit.
# - AL.K.15, AL.1.16, AL.2.16, AL.4.20: marked edited for added display types (Venn/yes-no charts, prediction, picture/bar graphs in gr 4);
#   arguably same. AL.3.16 edited for the added probability sub-standard.
# - AL.2.24 edited because it caps money problems at one dollar and drops dollar bills; AL.1.20 moved (coin identification from 2.MD.C.8).
# - AL.5.21 mapped to 5.G.B.4 as edited; triangle naming by sides/angles is not explicit in CCSS K-5 (could be read as new).
# - AL.3.20-3.23 split 3.MD.C.5/C.6/C.7 parts; AL.3.24 and 3.25 both map to 3.MD.D.8; AL.4.7/4.8 both map to 4.NBT.A.2.
# - PDF text is two-column; standards were read from the extracted text and spot-checked against the layout. Code numbers verified
#   contiguous per grade by the script.
